Physics_Units_Measurements.question: Which of the following is a base SI unit? (a) Newton (b) Metre (c) Joule (d) Pascal (e) Not sure
Physics_Units_Measurements.explanation: Metre is the SI base unit of length; Newton, Joule, Pascal are derived.
Physics_Units_Measurements.maps_to: Prerequisite: recognition of SI base units / Learning objective: identify base vs derived units

Physics_Units_Measurements.question: Significant figures in 0.00250 are: (a) 2 (b) 3 (c) 5 (d) 1 (e) Not sure
Physics_Units_Measurements.explanation: Leading zeros not significant; trailing zeros after decimal are.

Physics_Units_Measurements.question: Dimensional formula of force is: (a) [MLT⁻²] (b) [MLT⁻¹] (c) [MT⁻²] (d) [ML²T⁻²] (e) Not sure
A measurement of 2.5 cm has absolute error of 0.1 cm. Relative error is: (a) 0.04 (b) 0.4 (c) 4% (d) both a and c possible (e) Not sure
Which system is the modern standard for scientific measurement? (a) CGS (b) FPS (c) SI (d) MKS only (e) Not sure
Physics_Units_Measurements.explanation: SI is the International System of Units.

Mathematics_Sets.question: The empty set is denoted by: (a) {0} (b) ∅ or {} (c) {∅} (d) none (e) Not sure
Number of subsets of a set with 3 elements is: (a) 3 (b) 6 (c) 8 (d) 9 (e) Not sure
Venn diagrams are used to represent: (a) only unions (b) relationships between sets (c) only numbers (d) equations (e) Not sure
A set that contains all elements under consideration is called: (a) empty set (b) universal set (c) singleton (d) finite set (e) Not sure
Mathematics_Sets.explanation: Universal set is the reference set.

Accounting_Fundamentals.question: Accounting equation is: (a) Assets = Liabilities + Capital (b) Assets = Liabilities – Capital (c) Assets + Liabilities = Capital (d) none (e) Not sure
Which is a liability? (a) Cash (b) Creditors (c) Furniture (d) Stock (e) Not sure
Double-entry system means: (a) every transaction has two effects (b) only cash entries (c) single record (d) none (e) Not sure
Accounting_Fundamentals.explanation: Debit and credit for each transaction.

Accounting_Fundamentals.question: Capital is: (a) liability of business to owner (b) asset (c) expense (d) income (e) Not sure
Accounting_Fundamentals.explanation: Owner’s claim is treated as liability of the business entity.

Accounting_Fundamentals.question: Primary objective of accounting is to: (a) calculate tax only (b) provide financial information (c) market products (d) hire staff (e) Not sure

Political_Theory_Intro.question: Political theory primarily deals with: (a) only current elections (b) ideas and principles of politics (c) only economics (d) sports (e) Not sure
Political_Theory_Intro.explanation: Concepts such as freedom, equality, justice.

Political_Theory_Intro.question: Which is a core concern of political theory? (a) What is justice? (b) How to cook (c) Sports scores (d) Weather (e) Not sure
Political_Theory_Intro.maps_to: Learning objective: key questions in political theory

Political_Theory_Intro.question: Political theory helps us: (a) only memorise laws (b) critically examine political ideas (c) avoid politics (d) none (e) Not sure
Political_Theory_Intro.maps_to: Learning objective: purpose of studying political theory

Political_Theory_Intro.question: Freedom and equality are examples of: (a) physical objects (b) political concepts (c) mathematical terms only (d) none (e) Not sure
Political_Theory_Intro.explanation: Central political values discussed in theory.

Political_Theory_Intro.question: NCERT Class 11 Political Theory begins by introducing: (a) only Indian Constitution details (b) the idea of political theory itself (c) only foreign policy (d) none (e) Not sure
Political_Theory_Intro.explanation: Chapter 1 focuses on introduction to the subject.
Political_Theory_Intro.maps_to: Learning objective: orientation to the subject

Programming_Fundamentals.question: An algorithm is: (a) a programming language (b) a step-by-step procedure to solve a problem (c) a computer (d) a virus (e) Not sure
Programming_Fundamentals.explanation: Sequence of instructions independent of language.

A loop is used when: (a) you want code to run once only (b) you want to repeat a block of code (c) to declare variables (d) none (e) Not sure
Debugging means: (a) writing new code only (b) finding and fixing errors (c) deleting programs (d) none (e) Not sure

Business_Statistics_Intro.question: Descriptive statistics are used to: (a) make predictions about population only (b) summarise and describe data (c) only collect data (d) none (e) Not sure
Business_Statistics_Intro.explanation: Mean, median, graphs etc. describe the sample.
Business_Statistics_Intro.maps_to: Learning objective: role of descriptive stats

Business_Statistics_Intro.question: Which is a measure of central tendency? (a) Range (b) Mean (c) Variance (d) Standard deviation (e) Not sure
Business_Statistics_Intro.explanation: Mean, median, mode are central tendency measures.

Business_Statistics_Intro.question: Primary data is: (a) collected by someone else earlier (b) collected first-hand for the purpose (c) always numerical (d) none (e) Not sure
A frequency distribution organises data by: (a) alphabetical order only (b) how often values occur (c) random order (d) none (e) Not sure
OpenStax Introductory Business Statistics starts with: (a) advanced regression only (b) introduction to data and statistics in business context (c) only calculus (d) none (e) Not sure

Microeconomics_Intro.question: Microeconomics studies: (a) national income aggregates mainly (b) individual units such as consumers and firms (c) only international trade (d) none (e) Not sure
Microeconomics_Intro.explanation: Focus on individual decision-makers and markets.
Microeconomics_Intro.maps_to: Learning objective: distinguish micro vs macro

Microeconomics_Intro.question: The basic economic problem is: (a) unlimited resources (b) scarcity of resources relative to wants (c) too much production (d) none (e) Not sure
Law of demand states that, other things equal, when price rises: (a) quantity demanded rises (b) quantity demanded falls (c) demand curve shifts right (d) none (e) Not sure
Opportunity cost is: (a) the money cost only (b) the value of the next-best alternative forgone (c) total cost (d) none (e) Not sure
Market equilibrium occurs where: (a) demand exceeds supply always (b) quantity demanded equals quantity supplied (c) price is zero (d) none (e) Not sure
Microeconomics_Intro.explanation: Intersection of demand and supply curves.

Literary_Analysis_Intro.question: Literary analysis involves: (a) only summarising the plot (b) examining how elements work together to create meaning (c) rewriting the story (d) none (e) Not sure
Close reading means: (a) reading quickly (b) careful attention to language, structure and detail (c) skipping chapters (d) none (e) Not sure
Literary_Analysis_Intro.explanation: Detailed examination of the text itself.

Literary_Analysis_Intro.question: Theme in a literary work is: (a) the main character’s name (b) an underlying idea or message (c) the setting only (d) none (e) Not sure
When analysing a short story, one useful first step is: (a) ignore the text and invent (b) note plot, characters, setting and language choices (c) only count words (d) none (e) Not sure
Literary_Analysis_Intro.explanation: Observe the building blocks before interpreting.

Literary_Analysis_Intro.question: A literary analysis essay typically requires: (a) only personal opinion without evidence (b) claims supported by textual evidence (c) copying the story (d) none (e) Not sure
